sources.title: Getty Research Institute: Former Zhao / Han Zhao, AAT 300404601
sources.note: Institutional indexed original read in full through targeted search; direct open intermittently fails. Defines Southern Xiongnu state, 304-329, and alternate names. Imported dates/geometry come from local identity.json, not Getty.

sources.title: Hu Hong: Liu Yao’s life and northern cultures
sources.note: Original essay by Peking University historian Hu Hong, 8 July 2026; full page read. Sections on adoption, 304/308 foundation, 311/316 conquests, 318 succession crisis and final defeat. Literary superhuman descriptions and reconstructed romantic emotions not adopted as facts.

sources.title: Wu Honglin: Choosing Han and Zhao as dynastic names
sources.note: Original journal abstract and author metadata read through indexed institutional page; direct open fails. Journal of Shaanxi Normal University 2013(4), pp. 169-174. Used only for name, identity and political precedent claims stated in abstract.

sources.title: Zhuang Jinqiu and Cui Mingde: Han-Zhao’s relations with the two Jin regimes
sources.note: Original journal abstract read, direct metadata and indexed abstract. Journal of Northwest University for Nationalities 2010(4), pp. 103-110. No claim to have accessed complete article.

sources.title: Dong Gang: The jade prophecy of Liu Yao’s Guangchu fourth year
sources.note: Original Academic Monthly article, 2021, full HTML read. Sections 1-2: 318-319 succession, capital/name change, competing Zhao regimes, 321 prophecy and disputed interpretation. Reported jade is textual tradition, not an excavated object inspected here.

sources.title: Xi’an archaeologists report the Xiangjisi village cemetery
sources.note: Original reporting by Zhao Zhengyao, Sanqin Metropolitan Daily, 7 September 2019, quoting Xi’an Municipal Institute of Cultural Relics Preservation and Archaeology; full article read. Distinguishes M7, late Western Jin through Former/Later Zhao, from later Former Qin M1-M6. Subsequent excavation report bibliographically confirmed in Cultural Relics of Central China 2021(1), pp. 34-48,145; full report not accessed.

sources.title: Chen Feng and colleagues: Isotope evidence for Sixteen Kingdoms diets in Guanzhong
sources.note: Original 2025 paper, Scientia Sinica Terrae 55(10), pp. 3477-3488; indexed publisher abstract and introductory text read. DOI 10.1360/SSTe-2025-0042. Abstract reports 36 bone samples from 25 individuals, millet-dominant diet with C3 foods and/or animals. Broad Sixteen Kingdoms sample includes later burials; no narrow Han-Zhao attribution.

sources.title: Lin Yao-lin: Confucian thought and practice during the Sixteen Kingdoms
sources.note: Original university journal PDF read. Kaohsiung Normal University Journal 46 (2019), pp. 27-47; printed p. 31 / PDF page 5 quotes schools, ages, students and appointments. Author identifies official-historiographic ethnic prejudice in abstract.

sources.title: Gu Nong: Literary evidence in the Spring and Autumn Annals of the Sixteen Kingdoms
sources.note: Original scholar’s essay in Zhonghua Dushu Bao, reproduced by Chinese Writers Association, 23 April 2021, full text read. Sections 1-2 explain lost annals and Liu Cong’s lost poems; Chen An song received into court. Essay dates Chen An differently from other chronologies, so no point-year attached to that anecdote. No song lyrics reproduced.

sources.title: Book of Jin, juan 103: Liu Yao
sources.note: Public-domain transmitted primary history, compiled under Tang in seventh century, modern typeset transcription read directly. Exact passages: clothing/harvest/cattle rules; final defeat, wound physician Li Yong and message to Liu Xi. No original 329 manuscript claimed. Translation and modern pinyin in writing witness are editorial; primary wording checked against Shidian Guji chapter 1kz7cgbbdc2dr.

proposedOverrides.name: Han-Zhao / Former Zhao
proposedOverrides.summary: A Southern Xiongnu-led northern Chinese state, historically 304-329; its imported outline and dates are approximate.

batchIdentityNotes.decision: One exact indexed record only; no aliases. Southern Xiongnu-led Han founded 304, renamed Zhao under Liu Yao in 319, conquered 329. Distinct from Han Dynasty, broader Sixteen Kingdoms card and Shi Le’s Later Zhao.
batchIdentityNotes.mapEvidence: HB world-300.json feature from 300 to 400. Decoded bbox [105.63765637656377,35.620297347393176,112.420124201242,42.380598561702925]; northern shape excludes Chang’an and Luoyang and cannot represent changing imperial reach. Public overview explicitly warns.
batchIdentityNotes.dateDecision: Preserve imported map span in override; historical periods 304-310,310-318,318-329 in narrative. No invented date for broadly dated M7 or pooled diet sample.
batchIdentityNotes.writingDecision: No authenticated surviving Han-Zhao inscription identified in checked sources. Use expressly later-transmitted Chinese letter excerpt attributed to Liu Yao after capture in 329; seventh-century compilation, modern type and editorial translation/modern Mandarin labelled.
batchIdentityNotes.limits: Tomb M7 dates broadly late Western Jin through Former/Later Zhao. Isotope study covers wider Sixteen Kingdoms, including later burials. No routine family medical or sanitation practice extrapolated from royal wound treatment. No claim that reported jade prophecy is an excavated surviving artifact.
